title: A virtual metrology-driven tool-to-tool matching: toward early anomaly detection and diagnosis

abstract: A Tool-to-Tool Matching (TTTM), also known as chamber matching, is essential for stable fab operations. Still, physical metrology is sparse and requires a considerable amount of time to reach statistical significance, thereby delaying anomaly detection and diagnosis, and limiting the application of physical metrology-based TTTM. We present a virtual metrology (VM)-driven TTTM framework that produces predictions for each wafer in near real-time, enabling rapid chamber-level monitoring and early detection of mismatches. Dense outputs support statistically robust analysis, and model explainability identifies contributing inputs to guide root cause analysis. We propose a novel chamber mismatch score that quantifies discrepancies across chambers and enables reliable identification of anomalous chambers. We show that this mismatchbased monitoring allows earlier detection of chamber-level abnormalities and provides interpretable insights into potential causes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our VM model with adaptive online learning reproduces chamber-wise distributional patterns observed in physical metrology more accurately. Taken together, our framework enables earlier, statistically grounded monitoring at the chamber level and provides practical diagnostics for production fabs.
